about: Catalogue of analyses and interventions for the GM atrium overheating problem: what the app already covers and what is missing. status: in_sweep = simulated in data/sweep.json; proxy = estimated in js/model.js; missing = not modelled. how: e+ = add to tools/sweep_atrium.py and re-run; js = compute in the browser from existing data; external = needs another engine (Radiance, CFD). Ranges are suggested starting points, costs and carbon are deliberately null until sourced. now.level: yes = answered by the simulated results; partial = exact method but limited scope; approx = simple physics on current results (labelled in the app); no = needs new simulation or data, kept listed. Mechanisms live in js/mechanisms.js.

analyses.name: Hourly heat balance of the atrium
analyses.question: Is overheating driven by solar gain, too little ventilation, or concrete that never cools at night - and at which hours?
outputs: Zone Windows Total Transmitted Solar Radiation Energy
Zone Infiltration Sensible Heat Gain Energy
Zone Infiltration Sensible Heat Loss Energy
Surface Inside Face Conduction Heat Transfer Energy
Zone Electric Equipment Convective Heating Energy
analyses.app_view: Stacked hourly bars for the hot week; pick a design and an hour to see where the heat goes

now.how: Weekly balance rebuilt from results: solar = EnergyPlus, gains = model input, ventilation and glass conduction from hourly operative vs outdoor, remainder = thermal mass + error (H.heatBalance)
now.limits: Operative stands in for air temperature; opaque panels ignored; weekly totals only. Exact per-flow values need the E+ outputs listed above.

analyses.name: Transmitted solar per glazing element
analyses.question: Which part of the roof or clerestory lets in most heat - where should shading go first?
outputs: Surface Window Transmitted Solar Radiation Energy (per aperture)
analyses.notes: Name apertures by group (RS, RN, S, N, E, W) in build_model so results can be summed per element. The Ladybug radiation view shows exposure, not heat admitted.

now.how: EnergyPlus transmitted solar split by each element's share of Ladybug hot-week incident radiation (H.solarByElement)
now.limits: Same g on every element; angle-dependent transmittance ignored. Exact split needs per-aperture E+ output.

analyses.name: Night cooling of the thermal mass
analyses.question: Does the concrete actually cool overnight, or is night ventilation wasted?
outputs: Surface Inside Face Temperature (internal mass, floor, mass walls) at 07:00 and 18:00

now.how: Operative before opening and overnight drop from EnergyPlus hourly results (H.nightFlush; metric "Atrium before opening")
now.where: Diagnose + metric in Explore, Trade-offs, Sensitivity
now.limits: Concrete surface temperatures are not exported, so operative is used.

analyses.name: CIBSE TM52 adaptive overheating criteria
analyses.question: Does the design pass the UK standard test (hours of exceedance, daily weighted exceedance, upper limit)?
inputs: climate.json dry_bulb.future for running mean temperature
analyses.notes: Possible now for the hot week; a real TM52 test needs May-September, see summer_season.

now.how: All three TM52 criteria from EnergyPlus hourly operative, Category II, running mean from the 2050 file (H.tm52; metric "TM52 criteria failed")
now.where: Diagnose + metric in Explore, Trade-offs, Sensitivity
now.limits: Hot week only; criterion 1 is defined over May–September, so this is a stress test, not a compliance result.

analyses.name: Whole cooling season instead of one heatwave week
analyses.question: Does a design that survives the peak week still overheat across the summer?
analyses.notes: About 20x longer per run; sample the design space rather than the full grid.

now.limits: E+ results cover one week. Needs a longer RunPeriod in sweep_atrium.py (climate.json already has 8760 h outdoor data).

analyses.name: Several weather files and climate projections
analyses.question: Is the best design still best in other years and under real 2050/2080 projections?
inputs: CIBSE DSY1-3 or UKCP18-morphed EPWs for Manchester
analyses.app_view: Score ranges (min-max over weather files) instead of single values

now.limits: One weather file in the sweep. Needs re-running with more EPWs.

analyses.name: Vertical temperature stratification
analyses.question: How much hotter are the upper galleries than the well-mixed average?
analyses.notes: Split the atrium into 3-4 stacked zones joined by air walls, or use RoomAirModel; check a few designs with CFD (external).

now.limits: Single well-mixed zone; no data on vertical gradients. Needs stacked zones or CFD.

analyses.name: Wind- and stack-driven airflow
analyses.question: Can real openings deliver the assumed air-change rates on a still, hot afternoon?
analyses.current: Fixed ACH in the sweep; vent area is a stack-only proxy in js/model.js (ventArea)
analyses.notes: ZoneVentilation:WindandStackOpenArea or the Airflow Network, driven by opening area and height difference.

now.how: Hourly stack flow through an assumed installed free area vs the design ACH (H.stackAch; metric "Hours stack vents meet day ACH"), plus the existing vent-area proxy
now.limits: Stack only, no wind; uses temperatures from the fixed-ACH run, not coupled. Free area is an editable assumption.

analyses.name: Comfort with elevated air speed
analyses.question: How many degrees of relief do fans or cross-flow give occupants?
inputs: assumed air speed, clothing, metabolic rate
analyses.notes: SET or ASHRAE 55 elevated-air-speed method; ladybug-comfort has the equations.

now.how: ASHRAE 55 elevated-air-speed allowance subtracted from occupied-hour operative (H.fanCooling)
now.limits: Assumes fans reach every occupant; fan energy not counted.

analyses.name: Spatial daylight and glare
analyses.question: Which shading designs keep the atrium usefully daylit without glare or sun patches?
analyses.current: BRE average daylight factor proxy (daylightFactor in js/model.js)
analyses.notes: Radiance via Honeybee: sDA/ASE on the floor and galleries, DGP at key views. Run per shading option, not per full grid.

now.how: Existing BRE average daylight factor proxy
now.limits: No glare, sun patches or spatial distribution. Needs Radiance.

analyses.name: Winter heating including lost solar gain
analyses.question: How much winter benefit does low-g glazing or a fixed screen give away?
analyses.current: Conduction-only winter loss proxy (winterLoss); solar gain ignored
inputs: radiation.json annual results for atrium_roof faces

now.how: Conduction loss minus useful solar: Ladybug annual incident on the atrium glass × share falling in heating hours × g × frame × utilisation (H.winterSolar; metric "Winter glass loss − useful solar")
now.limits: Present-day temperatures, screen retracted, utilisation factor is an assumption.

analyses.name: Fan, cooling and electric-lighting energy
analyses.question: What does each intervention cost to run?
analyses.notes: Ideal loads for cooling energy; lighting from daylight results; fan power from ACH and pressure drop.

now.how: Cooling to hold 26 °C = (ventilation + glass conductance) × excess (H.coolingNeed); night-purge fan energy = SFP × flow × hours (H.nightFanKwh)
now.limits: Steady state, ignores thermal mass; lighting energy not covered.

analyses.name: Capital cost and embodied carbon
analyses.question: What does each intervention cost in money and kgCO2e?
analyses.notes: Fill cost_gbp_per_unit and carbon_kgco2e_per_unit in the interventions below from a sourced database (e.g. ICE, SPONs).

now.how: Quantities from the design × rates in this file (H.costCarbon)
now.limits: Mechanism ready; every rate is null until sourced, so the app says which rates are missing.

analyses.name: Heat exchange with the surrounding building
analyses.question: Does the atrium dump heat into, or receive heat from, the galleries and offices?
analyses.notes: Currently adiabatic walls. Replace with adjacent zones or a measured/assumed boundary temperature.

now.limits: Walls are adiabatic in the E+ model. Needs adjacent zones or boundary temperatures.

now.how: Sweep lever, EnergyPlus results
now.limits: Grid 0.2–0.7; interpolated between levels with measured error.

interventions.name: Glazing thermal transmittance
interventions.notes: Effect changes sign with shading: a better U-value traps heat when unshaded.

now.how: Sweep lever, EnergyPlus results
now.limits: Grid 1.0–5.8 W/m²K.

interventions.name: Daytime ventilation rate
interventions.notes: Fixed rate - see vent_opening_area for whether it is achievable.

now.how: Sweep lever, EnergyPlus results
now.limits: Fixed rate; achievability checked by the stack metric.

interventions.name: Night purge ventilation
trade_offs: security of open vents at night

now.how: Sweep lever, EnergyPlus results; fan energy if mechanical (proxy)
now.where: Explore designs + metric in Explore, Trade-offs, Sensitivity
now.limits: Fixed rate, no temperature control of the openings.

interventions.name: Static external roof screen
interventions.model: Horizontal shade 1.5 m above the ridge, constant transmittance

now.how: Sweep lever, EnergyPlus results
now.limits: Static, uniform plane.

interventions.name: Controlled or moving external roof shading
interventions.model: Shade transmittance schedule driven by solar radiation, or WindowShadingControl ExteriorShade with OnIfHighSolarOnWindow
interventions.why: Keeps winter and dull-day daylight that a static screen throws away

now.how: In hours with sun above the trigger, the operative temperature of the screened design is used; daylight reduced by the share of daylight hours deployed
now.limits: Ignores heat stored before deployment and control lag.

interventions.name: Internal roof blinds
interventions.why: Cheap retrofit; much less effective than external shading because the heat is already inside - worth showing that

now.limits: Inside the glass: needs WindowShadingControl in E+.

interventions.name: Reduce glazing on the south roof slope (opaque or insulated panels)
interventions.model: Scale glazing_m2 on south roof faces in zone_faces() / atrium_geometry.json
interventions.why: The south slope carries the largest glazed area (626 m2) and the highest exposure

now.how: Mapped to an equivalent g using the south slope's share of incident solar (53%), then the sweep is interpolated
now.limits: Conduction change through new opaque panels ignored; clamped at the lowest simulated g.

interventions.name: Fritted or PV-integrated roof glazing
interventions.model: Reduce effective g and VT on roof apertures; PV yield from radiation.json results
interventions.why: Turns part of the solar problem into generation

now.how: Equivalent g as above, plus PV yield = annual incident on roof glass × coverage × yield factor
now.limits: Frit treated as opaque; PV temperature losses and wiring not modelled.

interventions.name: Openable vent area and height (high- and low-level)
interventions.model: ZoneVentilation:WindandStackOpenArea replacing the fixed-ACH Infiltration object
interventions.why: Replaces assumed ACH with what real openings deliver; links ventilation to a buildable design

now.how: Installed free area (editable assumption) drives the stack metric
now.where: Assumptions + metric in Explore, Trade-offs, Sensitivity
now.limits: Does not change the simulated temperatures; wind ignored.

interventions.name: Fan-assisted night purge
interventions.model: Fan-driven ZoneVentilation with a night schedule and minimum outdoor temperature

now.how: Thermal effect = ach_night sweep lever; fan energy = proxy metric
now.where: Explore designs + metric in Explore, Trade-offs, Sensitivity
now.limits: No minimum outdoor temperature control.

interventions.name: More exposed thermal mass
interventions.why: Only useful together with night purge - a good interaction to show

now.limits: Mass is fixed at 1000 m² in every run. Needs MASS_M2 as a sweep lever.
Needs the finite-difference heat balance in E+.

interventions.name: High-reflectance opaque roof finish
interventions.model: solar_absorptance of FF_Steel1 on the opaque panels

now.limits: Opaque panel absorptance is fixed in every run.

now.how: Steady-state shift of occupied-hour temperature = Δgains / (ventilation + glass conductance)
now.limits: No thermal mass, so an upper bound.

interventions.name: Ceiling or high-volume low-speed fans
interventions.model: No change to E+ temperatures; comfort benefit via elevated-air-speed method

now.how: Comfort allowance from air speed (see comfort_air_speed)
now.limits: Fan energy and coverage not modelled.

interventions.name: Mechanical or evaporative cooling (last resort)
interventions.model: Ideal loads air system with cooling setpoint; report cooling energy instead of overheating
interventions.why: Benchmark: shows the energy that passive measures avoid

now.how: Cooling-to-26 °C proxy metric
now.limits: Steady state; no system efficiency.

interventions.name: Move occupation away from the hottest zones
interventions.model: Report temperatures per vertical zone; no fabric change

now.limits: Needs stratification results.
